title: Validate PR5831 on Linux: 4.40x complete precision replay, full coverage
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Reproduce Ali Romman's [PR #5831](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5831) exact-integer precision replay on Linux with the original complete scientific coverage. Across the original six serial fresh-process measurements, the **wall median falls 28.363 to 6.440 seconds: 4.40x, or 77.30% less wall time**. The **CPU median falls 28.300 to 6.430 seconds: 77.28% less**. All samples are retained in the original baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline/baseline/candidate order.

This validates an existing backend on another host; it does not claim its construction. Every fast replay executes all **25,984 events and 799 coordinates**, complete original result checks, final signed coefficients/scores, sufficient guards, literal attaining fixtures and six original rejection controls. The separate full `--qualify` additionally compares the Fraction reference, every actual signed witness dictionary, ideal metadata and exact local weights, plus 120 dyadic programs / 4,240 events and three integer rejection controls. **Its cost is separate: 60.47 seconds normally and 63.86 seconds under optimization.** The 4.40x factor applies to the complete original production replay, not that expanded reference qualification.

The input archives, exact integer backend, four declared contract edits and original expected scientific records remain unchanged. The new package supplies source/coverage review, four pre-import corruption controls, bounded CPU/wall/RSS measurements, portable reproduction and export validation. Five framework assumptions, native gauges, reset implementation/fees, exact owned zero return, physical precision and selected kappa retain their status. Kappa research stays paused.

## Task and overlap

Explicit donor assignment; `replay-runtime` refined to independent Linux portability and cost validation of frozen PR #5831 head `7c5eb98e7439d778141d63e801e53d4cd7e1d587`, retaining source [PR #5826](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5826) `58f93cf41751920f3d6766a39caccc2974ce18b0`. [The pre-execution claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5831#issuecomment-6433618407) freezes the success/stop criteria. The author's [released handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-19209571) requests Linux reproduction. Its neighbouring rounded-gauge investigation has a different word and scope.

Canonical main at entry and the prepublication checkpoint is `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, priority revision 8. Targeted PR/body and source-comment searches found no competing Linux timing follow-up; relevant Discussion claims were read. The submission checkpoint also read [PR #5838](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5838), head `ed8ecd3af2409ba7b1dcee06f335c9f7217ad007`: it supplies a separate changed-source PR5830 gauge/error contract. Our frozen PR5826/5831 scope and 26/23/22 guards remain bound to their own source. This is bounded coverage, without an exhaustive novelty or unpublished-work claim. [PR #5832](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5832) targets a different frozen literal-interpreter replay and is not repeated here.

Only the new `research/p104-integer-linux-validation/` scientific package is added. It retains the complete official 13-file PR #5831 export as one authenticated archive at our own ancestor `61f76fd9b3772b1b38981ea1d5b332d73a80e73b`; pending predecessor Git objects are not runtime dependencies. The original seven provenance bindings were authenticated at intake. The initial shallow checkout lacked several exact commit/blob objects; fetching them resolved the transport gap without weakening any source check. Full-history preflight remains unavailable.

The branch carries the same exact test-only [PR #5761](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5761) dependency, source `ba8a9e640e1983f3c29993fefa3f46e8ed03313a`, with Ali Romman's original authorship and cherry-pick credit. It changes no scientific artifact.

## Validation

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, Linux x86_64, CPython 3.12.3, Intel Core i7-4790. Source authentication and full normal qualification precede timing expansion. First-pair wall/CPU savings exceed the declared 15% gate. All six complete scientific receipts match exactly; raw output retains the volatile runtime field. Baseline wall observations range 28.217–28.716 seconds, candidate 6.386–6.488. Kernel peak RSS maxima are 99.38 versus 98.73 MiB; sampled process-group peaks are recorded separately. The host was not reserved and OS caches were not flushed. Three observations per arm and a different host do not establish a universal factor or statistical confidence.

Four new controls corrupt the whole official export, nested source archive, explicit contract and declared edit seam. They reject at exact predicates before scientific modules import, normally and under `-O`. Original six semantic and three integer controls remain active. Full normal and optimized qualification agree on every scientific receipt field, including 55 coefficient-scale bits and the unchanged sufficient 26/23/22 guards.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-integer-linux-validation
```

This registered command runs source-custody controls and then **fresh full unchanged `--qualify`**, including the Fraction reference and all extra witness/finite checks. It is not a stored-evidence acceptance command. The README gives the bounded original-order six-process benchmark, with all measurements retained and qualification cost separate.

Every local command keeps the original 180-second source limit, with 1 GiB sampled process-group RSS, bounded output, no automatic retries and a 900-second cumulative full-scientific-work budget. Full runs are serialized. One sealed-export launcher invocation failed **before target entry** because a relative driver path resolved under the package directory. Its exit-2/empty-output/error receipt is preserved, diagnosed and charged to the cumulative cap. A separately labelled, manually corrected absolute-path attempt uses the same source, expected records and resource limits. This is not a discarded slow sample or a repaired scientific failure.

The sealed implementation passes full qualification under `-I -O -B`, empty PATH and an explicit authenticated import root in **60.26 seconds**; all **53 exported files** retain their bytes/modes. Complete normal/optimized/sealed scientific receipts agree. Nine scientific commands pass; the separate pre-target launch failure is retained and charged. All ten local attempts cost **289.30 seconds**, below the 900-second cumulative cap. Public receipts redact only local script paths; the failed stderr redacts its workspace prefix with original hashes retained. Scientific stdout is unfiltered.

Implementation export `48479b602545f27e9a35742938be2d5f2bd8459e` contains the measured runtime. Later changes are reports/evidence only. Publication head `3e5c1beb92e967d79b26728c31432c718b9d3e25`: all 70 committed package files/bytes/modes, immediate own-input ancestry and official export/input integrity pass; full-history provenance is not claimed. Hosted CI is a separate exact-head gate and will be recorded in the canonical handoff.

PROOF-REVIEW.md, COVERAGE.json, BENCHMARK.json, VALIDATION.json and evidence/ preserve the source bindings, all raw measurements, controls, complete scientific outputs, failed launch diagnosis and limitations. The original verifier's nested private scratch retains its original writable behavior; the immutable archive and outer read-only export are checked, without claiming a new nested-scratch enforcement mechanism.

The complete archives remain unchanged. New Linux review, custody controls, measurements and report: Chris R / Clear1nsight, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human/proof-kernel acceptance. Guard/custody mechanics follow [PR #5816](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5816), [PR #5818](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5818) and PR #5832. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Review the exact dyadic representation and complete-coverage argument before adopting the source's fast replay. A second Linux host may test the performance range. A changed word needs a fresh source-specific scale/operation contract and finite feasibility before construction; this validation makes no successor transfer. Physical native/reset/owned-return admission remains separate. This bounded engineering scope releases at the handoff and resumes no kappa construction, Work 1/2, feed, worker swarm or automation.
